variants.label: Boudica
variants.text:
Boudica doesn't ask. She doesn't explain. She stands.

Unbowed. Unbroken. Unforgiving.

This isn't a queen for ceremony.

A look that dares you to do something about it.

Come on then.

variants.label: Establishment
variants.text:
The old guard is gone. The uniform remains.

A bowler hat. An umbrella. A grin built for the front row, not the front bench.

Know your place.

variants.label: The Clerk
variants.text:
The system survives on silence. This is the voice that breaks it.

A stubborn refusal to be erased from the ledger.

The official files call it an anomaly. We call it the truth.

Try to archive this.

variants.label: Frequency
variants.text:
From a distance, a target. Up close, pure attitude.

Built from within. Look closer.

Tune in. Or don't.

variants.label: Roll Call
variants.text:
No symbols required. No emblems necessary.

Just the names of those who refused to back down.

The Rebel. The Firebrand. The Statesman. The Queen.

Class is in session.

variants.label: Issue_000
variants.text:
The mark, before anything else. The badge planted in the ground.

Black and chalk white.

This is where it started.

Bowler and brollies. Dry, institutional. Black only.
Refusal to be erased. Subtlest read in the range.
Names, quiz format. Strongest comment engine.
Caps. Permanently stocked add-on, not a hero.
Top of funnel. Brand-building only - never sells product.

open.heading: Open item - needs a decision
open.body: The live site carries product art named Tommy, Skull, Tea and Roundel. Brand Book v4 §5 lists Issue_001 as The Establishment, Boudica, The Clerk, The Frequency and Roll Call, with no Tommy or Tea entry. Either the site is ahead of the book or the book is ahead of the site.

items.title: We do not recruit
items.body: No "join", no "fight back", no "the resistance". The brand implies defiance; it never issues instructions. Anything that reads as a call to action about anything other than buying a shirt is out.

items.title: Not party political, not activist, not victimhood-driven
items.body: Straight from the "We Are Not" list. No parties, politicians, campaigns, current affairs, or grievance framing. Audience is 30–60 across class and political leaning - the moment the brand picks a side it loses half of them.

items.title: Banned words
items.body: System. Deploy. Weapon. Resistance. Revolution. Uniform. Also avoid surrender, armoury, conscription, arsenal. Cosy period texture is welcome instead - Home Guard, Quartermaster's, Dispatched, Field Manual.

items.title: Never explain the joke
items.body: No clarifying, no adding context, no backtracking in the comments. If a line needs a follow-up post to explain it, the line was wrong.

items.title: Claims must be evidenced
items.body: Anything tagged red on this page is a real-world claim - price, stock, limited runs, customer messages. UK advertising rules apply to organic posts too, not just paid.

items.title: Paid social is narrower still
items.body: Campaign-line led, one line, product or graphic carries it. Target on interests - British heritage, independent brands, history, dry humour. Never target political categories. Run Eased register in paid; keep House organic.

items.title: No people in brand imagery
items.body: Fixed rule across the brand world. No models, no hands, no wrists. Flat lay or ghost mannequin on concrete, steel, weathered surface. UGC is the one exception and it lives in stories, not the feed.

items.title: Hashtags: zero to two
items.body: Targeted only. No carpet-bombing. The feed should read as a coherent archive, not a rotating carousel.
